entries.title: Sewage-like pattern in coastal water
entries.text: Conductivity fell while turbidity rose and dissolved oxygen and ORP declined. In coastal water this combination is consistent with fresh water carrying organic material, such as a sewage release. Stormwater runoff looks similar but coincides with rain. Sensor data alone cannot confirm the source.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show the full marine sewage pattern at a marine, brackish or estuarine pod.

entries.requiredEvidence: In the same window: dissolved oxygen down, ORP down, turbidity up and conductivity down.
entries.limitations: Cannot tell sewage from stormwater without a rainfall record, and cannot detect bacteria.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Sewage-like pattern in fresh water
entries.text: Conductivity and turbidity rose while dissolved oxygen and ORP declined. In fresh water this combination is consistent with an organic input, such as a sewage release. Industrial discharges can also raise conductivity. Sensor data alone cannot confirm the source.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show the full freshwater sewage pattern at a freshwater pod.

entries.requiredEvidence: In the same window: dissolved oxygen down, ORP down, turbidity up and conductivity up.
entries.limitations: Cannot tell sewage from other organic or industrial inputs, and cannot detect bacteria.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Low-oxygen pattern
entries.text: Dissolved oxygen and ORP fell together while conductivity and turbidity held steady. This is consistent with oxygen being used up faster than it is replaced, a condition that can stress or kill fish.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show dissolved oxygen and ORP falling together with no rise in conductivity or turbidity.

entries.requiredEvidence: Dissolved oxygen and ORP both below this pod's configured thresholds in the same window; conductivity and turbidity not rising.
entries.limitations: A worn or fouled dissolved-oxygen sensor, or still water around it, can produce falsely low readings.

review.notes: v2's signature is dissolved oxygen near zero with negative ORP; the report rule fires on crossing the pod's configured thresholds, which may be well above zero. Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Natural cold-water events in coastal water
entries.text: In coastal water, cold, low-oxygen water rising from depth (upwelling) or arriving with internal tides can lower dissolved oxygen and pH naturally. If temperature fell at the same time, that points toward a natural explanation rather than pollution.

appliesTo.conditions: Dissolved oxygen fell at a marine, brackish or estuarine pod, or the user asks whether low oxygen in coastal water means pollution.

entries.requiredEvidence: A dissolved-oxygen decline at a coastal pod.
entries.limitations: Upwelling usually affects several nearby sites at once; one pod cannot show that.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Runoff-like pattern
entries.text: Turbidity rose together with a change in conductivity, a pattern consistent with runoff after rain. Comparing the timing with a local rainfall record is the main way to tell runoff from other inputs.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show a turbidity rise together with a conductivity change.

entries.requiredEvidence: Turbidity up and conductivity changed in the same window, without a dissolved-oxygen and ORP decline.
entries.limitations: Without a rainfall record, runoff cannot be told apart from dredging, construction or other discharges.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Warming with falling oxygen
entries.text: Temperature rose while dissolved oxygen fell and the other readings held steady. Warmer water holds less oxygen, so this pattern is consistent with a warm-water discharge or with regional warming, such as a heat wave, or a marine heatwave in coastal water. Warming alone explains only a modest drop; a larger fall suggests oxygen is also being consumed.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show temperature up and dissolved oxygen down with no other reading moving.

entries.requiredEvidence: Temperature up and dissolved oxygen down in the same window; conductivity, pH, ORP and turbidity steady.
entries.limitations: One pod cannot tell a local discharge from regional warming; a heatwave affects a wide area and can last from days to months.
sources: sot-v2 §6.2 (thermal discharge and marine heatwave rows)

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Acid-like pattern in fresh water
entries.text: pH fell while conductivity rose. In fresh water this pairing is consistent with an acidic input, such as acid drainage or a chemical spill.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show pH down and conductivity up at a freshwater pod.

entries.requiredEvidence: pH down and conductivity up in the same window at a freshwater pod.
entries.limitations: Sensor data cannot identify the substance or its source.

review.notes: No marine entry on purpose: v2 §6.3 says acidic input is unlikely to be detectable in seawater unless near the source, so a marine report leaves this cause unnamed. Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Saltier water reaching the pod
entries.text: Conductivity rose while the other readings held steady. This is consistent with saltier water reaching the pod, for example on a high tide, during a dry spell, or with a storm surge. At coastal sites, tides can cause this routinely.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show conductivity rising with no change in dissolved oxygen, ORP, pH or turbidity at a marine, brackish or estuarine pod.

entries.requiredEvidence: Conductivity up in the same window, with dissolved oxygen, ORP, pH and turbidity steady.
entries.limitations: Without tide or rainfall records, cannot be told apart from a discharge that only raises conductivity.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Abrupt change with no clear pattern
entries.text: Conductivity, pH or ORP changed abruptly and did not match any more specific pattern this report checks for. Possible causes include a discharge from a nearby outfall or site, a spill, or a sensor fault. The data cannot tell which.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show an abrupt step change in conductivity, pH or ORP that matches no more specific pattern.

entries.requiredEvidence: An abrupt change in conductivity, pH or ORP in the same window.
entries.limitations: This is a low-confidence, catch-all pattern; it does not show that a discharge happened.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Daily oxygen swings consistent with algae
entries.text: Dissolved oxygen swung from a daytime high to a low before dawn, with pH moving in step. This daily pattern is consistent with heavy algal growth. The low point before dawn is when fish are most at risk.

appliesTo.conditions: A report event, or tool results, show large in-phase daily swings in dissolved oxygen and pH.

entries.requiredEvidence: Within one day, dissolved oxygen above and below this pod's configured thresholds, with pH swinging in phase.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot identify algae species or detect toxins, and toxin-producing blooms may show no oxygen pattern.

review.notes: The report cannot raise this event on live data yet: it needs a daily-cycle classifier that does not exist. Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: What the sensors cannot detect
entries.text: These sensors cannot detect bacteria, viruses, nutrients, metals or algal toxins, and can barely detect oil, so they cannot show whether the water is safe for swimming, fishing or shellfish harvest. Only appropriate testing, together with your local health agency's advice, can.

appliesTo.conditions: A sewage, runoff or algae pattern was found, or the user asks whether the water is safe or contaminated.

entries.requiredEvidence: None beyond the trigger or question.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Rule out the instrument first
entries.text: A sensor problem can look like a water-quality change. A single isolated point, a reading stuck at the same value for a long time, or every reading changing at the same instant are more likely signs of a sensor or connection problem. A real event more often shows a combination of readings that fits a physical explanation and lasts across several readings.

appliesTo.conditions: A reading crossed a configured threshold, or the user asks why a reading changed suddenly.

entries.requiredEvidence: A threshold crossing or an unexplained change.
entries.limitations: The report does not yet run automatic fault checks, so this is a caution, not a finding.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Turbidity is a relative clarity level
entries.text: Turbidity is shown as a relative clarity level (Clear, Moderate or Turbid), not a calibrated measurement, so it shows whether the water became cloudier but not by exactly how much. A long run of readings stuck at 0 (which looks like clear water) or at 1005 (which looks like very cloudy water) is the sensor's default for a bad reading or a failed sensor. Contact Clean Earth Rovers support to have the sensor replaced.

appliesTo.conditions: A pattern involving turbidity was found, the user asks what a turbidity value means, or turbidity has stayed at 0 or 1005 for an extended period.

entries.requiredEvidence: A turbidity reading or a turbidity change.
entries.limitations: A short run of 0 can be genuinely clear water; only a sustained run of the same value points to a failed sensor.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Alert limits are not healthy ranges
entries.text: This pod's alert limits start from Clean Earth Rovers defaults and may have been adjusted for the site. They are alert points, not health standards, so a reading inside them is not necessarily healthy for aquatic life. A limit set wider than the sensor can read will never raise an alert.

appliesTo.conditions: The user asks whether a reading within the pod's limits is safe or normal, or why no alert was raised.

entries.requiredEvidence: The pod's configured thresholds.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Readings from more than one location
entries.text: Pods are sometimes moved between sites. Readings taken before a move describe a different body of water and should not be compared directly with the current site.

appliesTo.conditions: The readings in the requested period come from more than one location, or the user asks about the pod's long-term history.

entries.requiredEvidence: Readings whose recorded location changes within the period.
entries.limitations: The pod's records do not note when it moved, so a move is inferred from its reported position.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Inspect the pod
entries.text: Inspect the sensors for fouling or damage and check that the pod is sitting properly in the water, so an instrument problem can be ruled out. Clean the sensors only if you can do so safely and within your site's safety rules; if a sewage, bloom or chemical release is suspected, avoid touching the water. If the battery is low or a sensor looks damaged, contact Clean Earth Rovers support. Don't let this delay other steps if people, pets or fish may be at risk.

appliesTo.conditions: A reading crossed a configured threshold or changed unexpectedly.

entries.requiredEvidence: A threshold crossing or an unexplained change.
entries.limitations: Cleaning resets fouling, so compare readings before and after.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Check power and connection
entries.text: If readings stop arriving, the battery runs low, or a reading stays stuck at one value, contact Clean Earth Rovers support; power, connection and sensor faults are handled by CER under your subscription. Don't treat the gap or the stuck value as a change in the water.

appliesTo.conditions: The user asks about missing, delayed or unchanging readings.

entries.requiredEvidence: A gap in readings, or readings that do not change.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Keep sensors calibrated
entries.text: Clean Earth Rovers calibrates the sensors as part of your subscription; routine cleaning between visits is up to you. Readings drift between calibrations, so a slow change over weeks can be drift rather than a real trend. If you suspect drift, contact Clean Earth Rovers support.

appliesTo.conditions: The user asks whether readings can be trusted, or about drift or calibration.

entries.requiredEvidence: None beyond the question.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Check the dissolved-oxygen sensor
entries.text: When dissolved oxygen is low, check the sensor alongside any response: clean it, and check that its reading changes when the water around it moves. If the reading still looks wrong, contact Clean Earth Rovers support to repair or replace it.

appliesTo.conditions: Dissolved oxygen is low, or the user asks what to do about low oxygen.

entries.requiredEvidence: Dissolved oxygen below this pod's configured minimum.
entries.limitations: Applies to the flow-dependent sensor type v2 describes; the pod's sensor type is not recorded in the registry.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Confirm with an independent measurement
entries.text: Ask a qualified person to confirm the flagged readings with an independent measurement, such as a calibrated handheld meter or a laboratory sample, before drawing conclusions. Avoid contact with water that may be contaminated.

appliesTo.conditions: A reading crossed a configured threshold, or the user asks how to check a reading.

entries.requiredEvidence: A threshold crossing.
entries.limitations: Sampling suspect water carries exposure risk, so use a trained sampler for sewage, bloom or chemical patterns.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Arrange bacteria testing
entries.text: Ask your local health or environmental agency, or a qualified sampler, to test the water for fecal indicator bacteria, such as Enterococcus in coastal water or E. coli in fresh water. Avoid contact with the water until results are available.

appliesTo.conditions: A sewage or runoff pattern was found.

entries.requiredEvidence: A sewage or stormwater event in the report, or the same pattern in tool results.
entries.limitations: Bacteria results take time; the sensors cannot stand in for them.

review.notes: Reworks the rejected draft 'sewage grab-sample': sampling is handed to a qualified sampler because of the exposure risk. Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Compare with rainfall
entries.text: Compare the time of the change with a local rainfall record. Runoff usually arrives within hours of rain.

appliesTo.conditions: A runoff or sewage pattern was found, or the user asks how to tell the two apart.

entries.requiredEvidence: A stormwater or sewage event.
entries.limitations: Rain earlier upstream can still arrive later; a dry day on site does not rule runoff out.

review.notes: The limitation reflects the v2 review concern (supervisor item 19) that Example 2's 'no rain rules out stormwater' goes beyond its observations. Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Compare with tides
entries.text: Compare the time of the change with local tide tables and recent rainfall. A rise that follows high tides or a dry spell makes saltwater more likely than a discharge.

appliesTo.conditions: A saltier-water pattern was found, or the user asks what caused a conductivity rise.

entries.requiredEvidence: A Saltwater intrusion event or a conductivity rise.
entries.limitations: Tide tables describe the nearest station, which may differ from the pod's site.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Compare with regional temperatures
entries.text: Compare with water temperatures from nearby monitoring stations or, in coastal water, regional sea-surface temperature reports. Warming across a wide area makes weather or a heatwave more likely than a local discharge.

appliesTo.conditions: A warming pattern was found, or the user asks whether warm water is local.

entries.requiredEvidence: A Thermal event or a temperature rise.
entries.limitations: Nearby stations may measure different depths or water.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Check for nearby activity
entries.text: Check for activity near or upstream of the pod at the time of the change, such as construction, dredging, pumping, outfall discharges or heavy boat traffic.

appliesTo.conditions: An unexplained or discharge-like change was found, or the user asks what could have caused it.

entries.requiredEvidence: An event without a confirmed cause.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Record what you see
entries.text: Note what you can see from a safe distance, such as water color, debris, dead fish or nearby work, with times and photos. Mention strong odors, but don't lean over or approach water you suspect is contaminated.

appliesTo.conditions: An event was found, or the user asks what to do next.

entries.requiredEvidence: An event in the report, or the user's question.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Keep watching the readings
entries.text: Keep watching the readings over the following days. A change that lasts across several readings or recovers gradually is more likely real. A single isolated point is more often a sensor glitch, but a brief spike can also be real, so note when it happened.

appliesTo.conditions: A reading crossed a threshold without a clear cause.

entries.requiredEvidence: A threshold crossing or an Inconclusive event.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Notify the responsible agency
entries.text: Notify your local sanitation or sewer agency or county environmental health office, or the agency named in your site protocol, and share the times and readings from this report.

appliesTo.conditions: A full sewage pattern was found.

entries.requiredEvidence: A sewage event at full-pattern confidence.
entries.limitations: The report does not know the site protocol or the responsible agency.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Treat very low oxygen as a priority
entries.text: Treat sustained low dissolved oxygen as a priority, check the sensor at the same time, and follow your site protocol for notifying others.

appliesTo.conditions: Dissolved oxygen stayed low for more than a few hours.

entries.requiredEvidence: A Hypoxia event lasting more than three hours.
entries.limitations: Check the sensor at the same time (see verify-do-sensor).

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Precautions for a suspected bloom
entries.text: Keep people and pets out of discolored or scummy water, and report a suspected bloom to your local environmental or health agency, which can test for toxins.

appliesTo.conditions: A report found the algae pattern, or the user describes a visible bloom.

entries.requiredEvidence: An Algal bloom event, or the user's description of a visible bloom.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot detect toxins.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Report a suspected discharge
entries.text: If a spill or unexpected discharge is suspected, report it to your local environmental agency with the times and readings from this report. If the only evidence is the readings, check the pod first.

appliesTo.conditions: A discharge-like pattern of at least Moderate severity was found, or the user suspects a spill.

entries.requiredEvidence: An Acidic input or Industrial event of at least Moderate severity.
entries.limitations: The data cannot confirm a discharge; the agency decides whether to investigate.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Report dead fish
entries.text: If you see dead or struggling fish, avoid handling them, note the time, place and approximate number, and report it to your state or local fish and wildlife or environmental agency. They may want to collect samples before anything is removed.

appliesTo.conditions: The user reports dead or struggling fish.

entries.requiredEvidence: The user's own report of dead fish.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot detect a fish kill.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: Share the report
entries.text: Share this report with the people responsible for the site, such as your site manager or monitoring team.

appliesTo.conditions: A report flagged a reading or an event.

entries.requiredEvidence: A flagged reading or event in a report.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Professional review for long events
entries.text: Consider asking a qualified water-quality professional to review this period.

appliesTo.conditions: An event lasted more than 12 hours, or the user asks who can investigate a problem outside the four CER services.

entries.requiredEvidence: A High-severity event, or an event lasting more than 12 hours, at or above the report's confidence floor.
entries.limitations: None.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: CER floating algae removal
entries.text: For a suspected bloom, follow your local agency's guidance first. Clean Earth Rovers can collect and remove floating algae.

appliesTo.conditions: A report found the algae pattern, or the user describes a visible bloom (discolored water, scum or mats) and asks for help removing it.

entries.requiredEvidence: An algal bloom event, or the user's own description of a visible bloom.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot confirm a bloom; this is a service offer, not a diagnosis.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: CER fish kill cleanup
entries.text: Once the responsible agency has been told and has had the chance to sample, Clean Earth Rovers offers fish kill cleanup.

appliesTo.conditions: The user reports dead fish and asks for help.

entries.requiredEvidence: The user's own report of dead fish.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot detect a fish kill.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.

entries.title: CER debris capture
entries.text: Clean Earth Rovers offers debris capture for floating trash.

appliesTo.conditions: The user asks about floating trash or debris in the water.

entries.requiredEvidence: The user's own description of debris.
entries.limitations: The sensors cannot detect debris.

review.notes: Approved as written, 2026-09-24.

entries.title: Oil spills and CER cleanup
entries.text: The pod's sensors largely cannot detect oil or fuel, so its readings cannot confirm or rule out a spill. If you see a sheen or smell fuel, report it. In the US, call the National Response Center (1-800-424-8802); in California, also call the Cal OES State Warning Center (1-800-852-7550). Elsewhere, contact your local environmental or maritime authority. Clean Earth Rovers can also help with small-to-medium spill cleanup.

appliesTo.conditions: The user reports an oil sheen, a fuel smell or a spill, or asks whether the pod can detect oil.

entries.requiredEvidence: The user's own report or question about oil.
entries.limitations: Oil barely changes the six measured readings.

review.notes: Approved with the edits proposed in the 2026-09-24 marked-up review.
